content.title: About
content.content: Flavored bran flakes are a whole‑grain breakfast cereal made from wheat bran, fortified with vitamins and minerals, and coated with a sweet flavored glaze. The flakes are crunchy and have a light sweet taste.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Bran is the outer layer of the grain and is rich in fiber and nutrients.
Flavored flakes often contain natural or artificial flavorings such as vanilla, honey, or berry.
There are many flavor options: berry, chocolate, vanilla, and more.
Bran helps improve digestion thanks to its high insoluble fiber content.
In several countries bran flakes are marketed as a “healthy” alternative breakfast.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Bran provides up to 25 % dietary fiber, supporting regular bowel movements and promoting satiety.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: The cereal contains thiamine, riboflavin, niacin, and folate, which are essential for energy metabolism.

items.title: Contains minerals
items.content: Bran flakes supply iron, magnesium, and zinc, important for blood health and nervous system function.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Unlike many sweet cereals, these flakes have minimal fat, making them suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Supports blood‑sugar stability
items.content: Fiber slows carbohydrate absorption, helping to prevent rapid glucose spikes after meals.

items.title: Added sugar
items.content: Flavored versions often contain added sugars, which may be undesirable for people with diabetes or those limiting calories.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: The product may contain milk, soy, or nuts, which can trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Wheat bran contains gluten and is not suitable for individuals with celiac disease.

items.title: Overconsumption
items.content: Large portions can lead to excess calorie and fiber intake, causing gastrointestinal discomfort.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Flakes can be eaten dry as a snack, but they are usually served with milk, yogurt, or a plant‑based beverage. Add fresh berries, nuts, or honey for extra flavor and nutrition.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the cereal in a sealed package in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, transfer to an airtight container to maintain crispness.

content.title: About
content.content: A fruit low‑fat muffin is a light baked treat made from whole‑grain flour, fresh fruit (such as apples, berries or bananas) and a small amount of plant oil or yogurt. It has a soft, moist crumb, a gentle sweet fruit flavor, and works well for breakfast or a snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Fruit muffins often incorporate whole fruit or puree, boosting vitamin and fiber content.
Low‑fat versions replace part of the oil with fat‑free yogurt or applesauce while keeping the batter moist.
Muffins originated in the United States but have quickly become popular in Europe and Russia.
Adding spices like cinnamon or ginger enhances aroma without extra calories.
Most recipes use baking powder and baking soda to create a light, airy texture.

items.title: Rich in vitamins
items.content: The fruit component provides vitamin C, vitamin A and B‑vitamins, supporting immunity and energy metabolism.

items.title: Good source of fiber
items.content: Whole‑grain flour and fruit increase dietary fiber, promoting healthy digestion.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Reduced oil content makes this muffin suitable for low‑fat dietary plans.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Fiber and antioxidants from fruit help lower cholesterol levels.

items.title: Moderate glycemic index
items.content: The combination of whole grains and fruit slows blood‑sugar spikes, beneficial for glucose control.

items.title: Allergy to ingredients
items.content: Some individuals may be sensitive to wheat, dairy, or specific fruits used in the recipe.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Even when sweetened with fruit puree, the recipe can still contain enough sugar for a sweet taste.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Despite low fat, whole‑grain flour and dried fruit add calories; portion control is advised.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the muffin as a standalone snack, split it and spread low‑fat cottage cheese, add it to yogurt, or use it as a base for a sandwich with lean cheese and greens.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store muffins in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days or in the refrigerator for up to 5 days. For longer storage, freeze in a zip‑lock bag – up to 3 months. Reheat in a microwave or oven before serving.
